Definition: from a compound of G3491 and G71; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively:--make (suffer) shipwreck.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns that some have put away faith and a good conscience and so made shipwreck of the faith, and he tells the Corinthians he has suffered shipwreck three times.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that faith can be wrecked like a ship: the conscience is the rudder, and once it is thrown overboard the faith founders on the rocks.
